name: Radon test kits and monitors
summary: Devices that measure radon, a radioactive soil gas that builds up indoors: mail-in test kits read by a lab, and battery digital monitors that show running averages.
uses: Radon is invisible and odourless, every home has some, and neighbouring homes differ: only a test shows a home's level (HC BROCHURE)
Canada's guideline is 200 Bq/m³ as a long-term average; above it, reduce it within a year, sooner if higher (HC GUIDE)
A valid test runs at least 3 months (91 days) and should fall in the heating season; radon changes from day to day, so short tests can mislead (HC GUIDE, C-NRPP CONSUMER)
It is the top cause of lung cancer in non-smokers, and radon with tobacco raises the risk significantly (HC BROCHURE)
Risk depends on the level and how long you breathe it, so a reading guides where to live and sleep, not an emergency escape (HC GUIDE)
identify: Mail-in kits: a small plastic detector (alpha track) with an expiry date, instructions and a lab return envelope; results come back in 3 to 6 weeks (HC GUIDE, HC ERM). Electret ion chambers are read with a calibrated reader, usually by a lab (HC GUIDE). Health Canada says DIY kits cost about $30 to $60 and are sold at home improvement stores (HC BROCHURE). Digital monitors: battery-powered units that show readings on a screen or an app (HC ERM). Models that passed C-NRPP testing include Airthings Corentium Home, Wave Plus and View Plus, and Ecosense RadonEye, EcoQube and EcoBlu; C-NRPP lists many other consumer models as not approved, and several were recalled (C-NRPP CONSUMER). Units: becquerels per cubic metre (Bq/m³) in Canada; US units are pCi/L, and 200 Bq/m³ is about 5.4 pCi/L (AIRTHINGS HOME). Screens show a short-term and a long-term average; judge by the long-term one after 3 months (HC ERM, AIRTHINGS HOME). The Corentium Home samples through a passive diffusion chamber, counts alpha particles, runs on 3 AAA alkaline cells and works from 4 to 40 °C (AIRTHINGS HOME). C-NRPP is the Canadian National Radon Proficiency Program; Health Canada strongly recommends testing only with devices on its list (HC GUIDE, C-NRPP CONSUMER).
test: Mail-in kits are useless without the lab that reads them; alpha track detectors must be used before their expiry date, and electrets need a reader (HC GUIDE). Digital monitors: fit fresh alkaline AAA cells, not rechargeables; a Corentium Home shows CAL while it checks its sensor and gives a first reading 6 to 24 hours later (AIRTHINGS LIFESPAN). Radon varies from day to day and week to week (C-NRPP CONSUMER), and Airthings gives its accuracy at 200 Bq/m³ as about 10% after 7 days and about 5% after 2 months (AIRTHINGS HOME), so judge a monitor over weeks, not hours. A model not on the C-NRPP list is unproven, and consumer monitors can't be professionally recalibrated (C-NRPP CONSUMER); Health Canada suggests replacing electronic monitors after about five years (HC GUIDE). Removing the batteries starts a fresh measurement, so note the readings first (AIRTHINGS LIFESPAN). Place it on the lowest lived-in floor, 0.5 to 2 m up, away from windows, doors, vents, outside walls, heat and electronics, and run it at least 3 months (HC ERM).

decay.note: Mail-in kits can't be read without a working lab; Airthings says a Corentium Home can work up to 10 years, but its 3 AAA cells last up to 2 years (AIRTHINGS LIFESPAN, AIRTHINGS HOME), and Health Canada suggests replacing electronic monitors about five years after purchase (HC GUIDE).

improvise: Health Canada says the only way to be sure of the radon level in a home is to test it (HC BROCHURE). Without a test, assume the lowest floors are worst: radon comes from the soil through foundation cracks, slab joints, gaps around pipes, floor drains and sumps, and is usually highest in basements and crawl spaces (HC BROCHURE, HC GUIDE). Radon is generally highest in basements and crawl spaces, so more time on higher floors may lower your exposure, but elevated levels can be found throughout a home (HC BROCHURE, HC GUIDE). If the house has an active soil depressurisation system (a pipe through the foundation floor to outside, with a fan that runs all the time), keep the fan running when you have power: it cuts radon by 90% or more (HC REDUCE). A heat-recovery ventilator run all the time cuts it by only about 20 to 50%, and sealing cracks helps it work (HC REDUCE). Don't smoke: radon and tobacco together significantly increase lung-cancer risk (HC BROCHURE). Risk builds with the level and the years of exposure (HC GUIDE), so this is a choice about where to live, not a reason to flee.
